 J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Mr.Adhit S/o.Sadanandan in road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 26.06.2019 at about 05.10 a.m., the deceased Mr.Adhit,
along with his friend, was travelling in Car bearing Regn.No.KL-11-AV-2040, from Ekarool towards Kodigehalli and when the car reached near B.M.Road, in front of RDC Concrete Factory,
Kumbalagudu, Kengeri Hobali, Bengaluru South Taluk, it dashed to a Cement Bunker Lorry bearing Regn.No.NL-01-L-3496, which had been negligently parked on the wrong side of the road without any precautionary measures.
Due to negligent parking of lorry by its driver, the car hit the lorry.
Due to the accident, the deceased succumbed to the injuries at the spot.
The petitioners have spent a sum of .1,00,000/- towards transportation and funeral obsequies ceremony etc.

Prior to the accident,
the deceased was hale and healthy and employed at Santhi Dama College of Nursing, Opp.
Kodigehalli Police Station, Kodigehalli, Magadi Road, Bengaluru, as Admission Co-ordinator and was drawing salary of .20,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their beloved son and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent parking of Cement Bunker Lorry by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.

3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 & 2 did not appear before the tribunal and hence,
they have been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.3 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.3 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.3 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.

Further the respondent No.3 has contended Sadanandan P.P vs Vinod Raj on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163708650/
2 that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further respondent no 3 admitted the aspect of issue of policy of insurance pertaining to the lorry and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the driver of car was solely responsible for the alleged accident.
Further the driver of lorry was in no way responsible for the alleged accident.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of car.
Further the driver of lorry was not holding valid and effective driving license and the lorry was not having valid FC and permit as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioners prove that the son of petitioner No.1 and 2 namely Adhit succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 26.06.2019 at about 05.10 a.m., B.M.Road of RDC Concrete Factory, Kumbalagudu Hobali,
Bengaluru South Taluk, Bengaluru, when he was proceeding in Car bearing Regn.No.KL-11-AV-2040 along with his friends, due to negligently parking of Cement Bunker Lorry bearing Regn.No.NL- 01-L-3496 by its driver?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to substantiate the contention of the petition, the Petitioner No.1/father of deceased got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed their evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 & 2 and closed their side evidence.

7. Heard the arguments of both side and perused the materials available on records.
8.

This Tribunal answers the above issues as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Negative.

9. Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioners that, deceased succumbed to the Sadanandan P.P vs Vinod Raj on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163708650/
3 injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 26.06.2019 at about 05.10 a.m., on B.M.Road in front of RDC Concrete Factory, Kumbalagudu, Kengeri Hobali, Bengaluru South Taluk, Bengaluru City, when deceased was traveling in a Car bearing Regn.No.KL- 11-AV-2040, due to the rash and negligent parking of Cement Bunker Lorry bearing Regn.No.NL-01-L-3496 by its driver.
10. The Petitioner No.1/father of deceased examined as PW.1.

In the chief-examination, PW.1 deposed that his son was traveling in the car which was going slowly and cautiously and due to rash and negligent parking of cement bunker lorry vehicle by its driver, the accident occurred.
In order to prove the accident and negligent parking of offending vehicle, the petitioners produced Ex.P.2, First Information statement lodged by father of deceased with police on 07.06.2024.
On the basis of first information lodged by 1st respondent, the police have registered FIR, as per Ex.P.1, for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Inquest Report.

Ex.P.4 is the PM report,
wherein it is mentioned that deceased Mr.Adith.S died due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained.
It is the contention of petitioners that the offending car was parked negligently due to which the accident occurred.
In the first information statement, there is no allegation of negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry in the cause of accident.
Though there is mention about parking of lorry in the first information statement, it is not mentioned that the lorry has been parked negligently and same is the cause for the accident.

On perusal of Ex.P.2,
first information statement, it could be noticed that respondent No.1 has lodged the first information statement before the police pertaining to the accident.
In the first information statement, it is stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.
The aspect of negligence for the cause of accident has been alleged against the driver of the car bearing registration No.KL-11-AV- 2040, in which deceased has been traveling.
The petitioners could have lodged complaint before the police pertaining to negligence of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident after they came to know about the same.
But, the petitioners do not appear to have made efforts to lodge the complaint to the police alleging negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
In first information statement, there is no allegation of negligence on the part of driver of lorry and allegation of negligence is only on the part of driver of car.
The petitioners could have challenged the contents of first information statement before the higher authorities or before the concerned court.
The recitals of first information statement are contrary to the contention of petitioners.
11. Further, the FIR furnished by petitioners discloses that same has been registered against the driver of car bearing registration No.KL-11-AV- 2040.
Ex. P.1
does not disclose the aspect of registration of FIR against the driver of offending lorry.
The FIR has been registered against the driver of car for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
The petitioners do not appear to have questioned or challenged the FIR registered by the police against the driver of car.
If the accident has been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle, then the petitioners could have questioned or challenged the FIR before appropriate authority.
The FIR discloses the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of car bearing registration number KL-11-AV- 2040 and not against the driver of offending vehicle.

The recitals of FIR are also against the Sadanandan P.P vs Vinod Raj on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163708650/
4 contentions of the petitioners.
12. The petitioners furnished inquest and post mortem report which discloses the aspect of death of Adith.
The aspect of death does not appear to be in dispute.
The inquest and post mortem report discloses the aspect of death of Adith in the accident.
13. The petitioners not furnished the final report filed by the police and same has been furnished by respondent No.3 which is marked as Ex.R.2.
The police have conducted investigation in the matter and after detailed investigation, filed final report against the driver of car.
In the final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of car rather than driver of offending lorry.
The final report is filed after detailed investigation and the police have not alleged negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry.

The recitals of final report disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of car in which the deceased was traveling and there is no allegation against the driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The petitioners do not appear to have questioned or challenged the final report filed against the driver of the car.

It is the contention of petitioners that the accident has been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of lorry but, the recitals of final report are contrary to the contentions of petitioners.

The police have filed the final report against the driver of car alleging negligence on his part in the cause of accident and the police have stated nothing with respect to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The police have not stated the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of vehicle in the cause of accident.
The police records do not disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
14. The contentions of petitioners are not substantiated by cogent and substantive materials.
The petitioners filed the present petition under Sec.166 of M.V.Act seeking compensation for the death of their son Mr.Adith.
The petitioners have to establish the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The provision under which the petitioners filed the claim petition casts burden on them to prove the aspect of negligence on the part of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The petitioners have not placed any materials in order to discharge the burden cast on them.

In order consider that the petitioners are entitled for compensation under Sec.166 of M.V.Act, they have to establish the aspect of occurrence of accident as well as negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Though the materials on record disclose the aspect of occurrence of accident, they do not disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
It is incumbent on the part of petitioners to establish negligence on the part of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
But, the materials placed by the petitioners do not disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The petitioners could have examined the person, who was traveling along with their son, in order to substantiate their contentions.
The petitioners not examined any witnesses in order to show that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The documents furnished by petitioners do not disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.

The petitioners could have also examined the driver of the car in order to show that there was negligence on the part of driver of the lorry and there was no negligence on the part of driver of the car.
The petitioners neither examined any witnesses to the accident nor made any efforts in that regard.

The petitioners have the right and Sadanandan P.P vs Vinod Raj on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163708650/
5 opportunity to examine either the driver of the car or the person going along with the deceased in the car.
But, the petitioners have not examined any persons in order to substantiate the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of lorry in the cause of accident.
The burden is on the petitioners to prove the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of lorry, but they have failed to discharge the said burden with cogent and substantive material.
The materials relied by petitioners itself disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of the car and are contrary to the contentions of petitioners.
The petitioners not examined any witnesses on their behalf who have noticed the accident or present at the time of accident.
The documents placed before the Tribunal discloses the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of the car.
The materials on record do not point out towards negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioners not furnished satisfactory materials in order to show the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of lorry in the cause of accident.
The petitioners failed to discharge the burden cast against them.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of the car in the cause of accident.
The negligence on the part of driver of lorry in the cause of accident is not forthcoming from the materials on record.
The petitioners failed to substantiate their contention with cogent materials.
Though the occurrence of accident is proved, the petitioners failed to prove that negligence of driver of lorry is the cause for the accident.
The burden is on the petitioners to establish negligence of driver of lorry in the accident, but they have failed to establish the same.
The petitioners asserted negligence on the part of driver of the lorry in the cause of accident, but failed to establish the said aspect with cogent materials.
The assertion of petitioners regarding negligence of driver of lorry is not substantiated by cogent and satisfactory materials.
Hence, on consideration of above stated aspects, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 in the Negative.
15. Issue No.2:- The petitioners failed to establish negligence on the part of driver of lorry, as contended by them.
As the petitioners failed to prove the aspect of negligence of driver of the lorry in the cause of accident, they are not entitled for compensation.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered in the Negative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed.
No order as to cost.
Office to draw Award accordingly.
